summary: The instrument works, and its two acceptance-shaped holes are closed or named. One harness drives four arms over one frozen trace (same sha256 per rung on every arm) at matched durability, each engine in its own 128 MiB scope, under one latency rule - the lag ceiling, the 3-consecutive-window growth clause and errors, bound by a test to flashdb-load's own verdicts - and every inventory oracle passes everywhere it was run, now including flashdb's 10x read-back (12 checks over 10.6M cells). At the pre-registered regime (flashdb 1.68 GB = 12.546x of the cap, one seed, the 1x rung) all three arms hold 50 rps with zero errors and T5's throughput deficit is 1.001 against the 1.5x line, and T7 with it; but that run was contended (loadavg 6.1-8.3): flashdb was rejected on 12 of 20 windows, sqlite on 1 (a 1.97 s stall) and postgres on 3, so NO arm sustained the rung there, while the earlier pre-fix run on the same seed and data had both baselines clean. T5's throughput reading therefore reproduces across both runs and its sustained reading does not: the T5/T7 verdict is not robustly determined and needs a quiet-box repeat. T6 at the regime - the actual external-superiority claim - remains unevaluated (no ladder at 10x). In the warm ladder T6's pre-registered comparison has no denominator at 400 rps (no baseline sustained that level), and the sustained-vs-sustained reading is 0.50x for the declared arm and 1.00x for the learned one against the 3x line, i.e. FAIL. No result here supports a claim that flashdb beats postgres or sqlite at scale, a claim about the learned arm (in M1 it is the declared wiring), or a claim about drift and reorg cost.
unverified: T6 at the pre-registered regime: it needs a ladder at >=10x, and one 10x flashdb arm-run costs 416 s of seeding plus a 38 min read-back at 10.6M cells; run B measured the 1x rung only.

The sustained-rule outcome at the regime rung is not robustly determined: the committed run B was measured at loadavg 6.1-8.3 on 8 cores and no arm sustained 50 rps (flashdb 12 of 20 windows rejected, sqlite 1 of 20 with a 1.97 s stall, postgres 3 of 20), while the earlier pre-fix run on the same seed and data (loadavg not recorded, its provenance defect) had sqlite and postgres clean and flashdb 1 of 20. A quiet-box repeat decides it.
The pre-registered 10-seed median/IQR aggregation: both runs are one seed.

Run A's rung-400 comparison: the SQL arms' windows were re-measured on 2026-10-17 at loadavg 2.2-4.1 rather than the 1.5-2.5 of the first ladder, so its numbers are a second measurement of the same traces, not the first one repaired.
